result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say the form is in good shape and find the same real bugs: the POST sends no body, and the code never checks res.ok. Both also rewrite most of the submit handler, which goes beyond a light polish. A keeps the palette and returns a complete drop-in version with the same IDs and classes. B changes the field border colour with a new CSS variable; the contrast point is valid but it alters the palette. B also gives only fragments, which leaves more merging for the user. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the form is in good shape and find the same real bugs: the request sends no data, server errors show as success, and the open days aren't checked. A changes the border color, which touches the palette. The contrast reason is valid, but the rubric asks for no palette changes. B leaves the styling alone apart from one small margin fix and returns a complete drop-in version that keeps every ID and class. Both rewrite the JS more than a light polish needs, and B also adds a few useful notes on what to check before shipping.
